description: Only transactions with an amount strictly greater than 2400 count, so an amount of exactly 2400 is excluded.

b.request: Find the 10 accounts with the most transactions with amount strictly greater than 2400, showing account ID, average amount of those transactions, and transaction count, sorted by count descending.
b.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(amount) as avg_amount, COUNT(*) as transaction_count FROM trans WHERE amount > 2400 GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10;
b.raw: Find the 10 accounts with the most transactions with amount strictly greater than 2400, showing account ID, average amount of those transactions, and transaction count, sorted by count descending.

d.request: Identify the 10 accounts with the highest count of transactions where trans.amount > 2400, showing for each the account_id, average trans.amount of those transactions, and count of such transactions, sorted by transaction count descending.
d.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(amount) as average_amount, COUNT(*) as transaction_count FROM trans WHERE amount > 2400 GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: Treating 2400 as the cutoff for a large transaction amount (`trans.amount`), which 10 accounts (`trans.account_id`) have the most large transactions? For each one, show the account ID, the average amount of its large transactions, and how many it has, sorted by that count from highest to lowest. Only transactions with an amount strictly greater than 2400 count, so an amount of exactly 2400 is excluded.
c.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(amount) AS average_amount, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM trans WHERE amount > 2400 GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: Considering only transactions whose amount (`trans.amount`) is greater than 2400, group them by account (`trans.account_id`) and, for each account, show the account ID, the average transaction amount, and the number of such transactions. Sort the accounts by that number of transactions from highest to lowest and return only the first 10.
a.sql: SELECT trans.account_id, AVG(trans.amount) as avg_amount, COUNT(*) as transaction_count FROM trans WHERE trans.amount > 2400 GROUP BY trans.account_id ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10;
